title: Finding a teacher
hookLine: check them over time, as the texts advise (MN 47)
tomorrow: what did one question on a street do for Sariputta?

lines: A NUMBER THAT SAYS TRUST ME.
A VISITING TEACHER, A GLOWING ROOM.
cards: Reviews, ratings, a follower count: online there's always a number telling you to trust this person. The Thursday sit has a visiting teacher this week, warm, funny, a story for everything, and the whole room is glowing.
Mai is too, a little. She also remembers Kosambi: people are people. There's a sutta for exactly this moment, and its answer fits in three words.

teach.b: In it, the Buddha tells his monks to investigate even him. Watch him with eyes and ears. Are there signs of greed or confusion in what he does and says?
Has he been well known for a long while, and has fame brought its dangers with it? Does he hold back from harm because he's afraid, or because the wanting is gone?
Only then, the sutta says, does trust have reasons under it. The teacher on trial is the Tathagata, the Buddha himself.
Now hold that up against the week. A year of holy days, kept with others. A place to go.
Friends who are the whole of it. Finding them, past the fear at the door. Showing up to lift the pot.
And now, checking first. None of it is suspicion. It's how a good friend gets chosen with open eyes.

how: Buddhist traditions advise getting to know a teacher over time before taking them as one's guide; people often attend talks and retreats with a teacher for a while, watching their conduct, before committing to them.

o: choosing whom to learn from by watching how they live
picking the teacher with the biggest following
a chanting test you pass before you can ordain

games.q: the test in MN 47 — tap the pairs.
p: watch what he does and says
from fear, or because the wanting is gone?

s: in this sutta, the Buddha exempts himself from being checked
he's the one the monks are told to investigate.
the sutta asks whether fame has changed the teacher
it asks whether he's been well known a long while, and whether its dangers came with it.
checking a teacher means being suspicious of everyone
it's watching with open eyes, so trust has reasons under it.

games.q: your mom's friend wants to join a meditation group led by a teacher she met once. she asks you what to look for. what fits the sutta?
o: how he acts over months, with money, praise and people who disagree
how deep his talks sound, since wisdom shows itself in words
how well-known he is, since fame means he's already been tested
games.why: the sutta checks conduct, seen and heard over time, and asks whether fame has brought its dangers. a talk is a start, not the test.

practice: On a scrap of paper, write three things you'd want to see in anyone you learn from, a teacher, a coach, a mentor. Not what they say: what they do, over time. Then rest with the list in your lap while the sit runs.

wordCard.voice: Finding a teacher: choosing whom to learn from by watching how they live over time, the way the Buddha asked to be watched.

orig.note: Pali: teacher; one who trains others in conduct and the path.

carryVoice: Your line: check first. Trust is better with reasons under it. A week of sangha, done.
